purpose: Pin where every codec regression input comes from, under which terms it may be used, which hash identifies it and which documented limitation a failing vector belongs to, so a fresh contributor can reproduce the r11 evidence without private media or an unpinned upstream checkout.

hash_pinning.corpus_identity: sha256 of the extracted input file consumed by tests/conformance.py
hash_pinning.upstream_checksum: md5 (source_checksum) of the upstream download, taken from the pinned suite file and verified before an asset is accepted; the pinned suite digest makes that value itself tamper-evident
hash_pinning.suite_definition: sha256 of the pinned Fluster suite file; a changed definition invalidates names, checksums and totals
hash_pinning.rule: A hash becomes an expectation only when a reviewer records it here. tests/corpus.py lock reports hashes and never edits this file.
hash_pinning.licence_rule: Each entry states whether usable terms were identified or not established (terms_status), where terms were checked (terms_reference, terms_checked) and what that implies. Nothing may be redistributed without an identified licence; 'not established' is recorded explicitly instead of inferred.

policy.redaction: Publishable manifests, logs and lock files carry no personal paths, media, tokens, process arguments or extracted core dumps.

fluster.note: Suite definitions are read from this pinned checkout. The r11 evidence was produced from an unpinned local checkout, which is recorded as a gap below.

known_issues.summary: Long-term reference handling for RPS_E still produces wrong output; short-term-only AVD ordering is preserved in decode order and long-term streams keep the original order.
known_issues.review: Recorded from the r11 M1 record; re-review when the HEVC reference handling changes.

known_issues.summary: Main 10 stream in the 8-bit configuration of the suite run: the 10-bit path must be enabled deliberately, and this is a capability boundary rather than a hardware failure claim.
known_issues.review: Confirm against a deliberate 10-bit run before changing the class.

known_issues.summary: FFmpeg's parameter-set parser loses pictures in this stream; direct GStreamer V4L2 passes it. Do not count it as a driver pass or a driver failure without the client name.
known_issues.review: Client-dependent; keep the client in the evidence.

known_issues.summary: Progressive Baseline/Extended streams that FFmpeg's profile selection rejects; they decoded bit-exact on the M1 with an explicit allow_profile_mismatch override.
known_issues.review: A per-file workaround for tested coding features, not Baseline/Extended support.

known_issues.summary: Interlacing, MBAFF, field pictures, FMO, ASO, data partitions and similar syntax are not implemented; the earlier parsing defects in these paths are fixed and the remaining gap needs work, not a new workaround.
known_issues.review: Re-review whenever H.264 syntax support changes.

known_issues.summary: High 4:2:2 output is outside the tested hardware formats; FFmpeg can silently fall back to software here, so these vectors are not hardware evidence either way.
known_issues.review: Only a supported 4:2:2 capability claim may remove this class.

known_issues.summary: High-profile syntax (interlacing, frame packing, data partitions and related features) is unimplemented; the opt-in High 10 path passes 27 of 69 FRExt vectors.
known_issues.review: Re-review with the FRExt evidence record.

known_issues.summary: Streams with a dimension below 64 pixels are rejected before submission; software passes them, so this is a decoder capability boundary, not corrupt input.
known_issues.review: Changing the minimum dimension is a support-contract change.

known_issues.summary: Profile 1 4:2:2/4:4:4 streams are outside the advertised VP9 profiles on the tested device (profiles 0 and 2).
known_issues.review: Tie any change to an advertised-profile change.

known_issues.summary: These two resize streams previously triggered firmware timeouts; userspace now rejects them without new kernel messages. Rejection is not decode support and the streams stay open in the roadmap.
known_issues.review: Decoding must not be claimed from the rejection.

known_issues.summary: Inter-frame resize checksums mismatch on AVD; full inter-frame resize support needs the kernel-side work tracked in the roadmap.
Scalable-video stream also misses its reference checksum in software, with a different digest: the comparison baseline itself is in doubt, so this must not be reported as a plain driver regression.
known_issues.review: Treat as a reference/software question first.

known_issues.summary: 12-bit and 4:2:2/4:4:4 high-bit-depth vectors are outside the tested hardware formats; the single 10-bit 4:2:0 vector is the r9 1/1 result.
known_issues.review: Only a supported-format change may remove this class.

smoke.description: Bounded subset a clean environment and CI can acquire: one representative per state a contributor has to reproduce (pass, expected rejection, known wrong output, unsupported format, capability boundary) plus the generated matrices. The budget bounds the extracted inputs that CI caches; the recorded cold run downloaded 20,809,931 bytes of upstream files and `fetch` reports that volume each time. Full suites stay on demand.

Multiview HEVC is not part of the r11 evidence.

known_gaps: The r11 pass sets were produced from an unpinned Fluster checkout. This manifest pins commit f3ad284a9e6cac70dc01b02e0de71c2994181d34 and verifies each suite file by SHA-256, so a re-run must state which pin it used; the totals above are only reproducible against a stated pin.

Per-vector SHA-256 is pinned for the smoke subset only. Other vectors are verified against the upstream source_checksum (MD5) from the pinned suite and receive a SHA-256 through `corpus.py lock`, which reports the value for deliberate review instead of editing this file.

The r11 records store pass/fail per vector but not the reason. The classifications here are derived from the pinned suites plus the documented notes; they are re-checked on every validate run against the pass sets, and drift fails the check.

On a macOS host the ITU (JVT/JCT-VC) archives were rejected by the distributor's request filtering, while the same URLs downloaded from an Ubuntu container. Contributors on macOS need a Linux environment or a mirror for those suites; the VP9 vectors downloaded from both.

Generated matrices are compared against software output recomputed locally rather than against committed hashes, because encoder output depends on tool versions and thread counts. A tool change is therefore visible as a new software reference, not as a silent pass.
No hardware-qualification evidence is produced by this manifest: it describes acquisition and provenance, not decoding support. Hardware runs stay in tests/hwguard.py with an exclusive lease.

Usage terms for the official vectors are recorded as not established: the ITU/JCT-VC and JVT bitstreams come from the ITU working file area whose copyright notice grants no reproduction right, and the WebM test-data directory carries no licence file. Nothing is redistributed here, and anyone redistributing them must settle terms with the distributor first.

Pinning a vector's SHA-256 is separate from acquiring it: `fetch --suite`/`--all` enumerate the pinned suite definition (see `fetch --dry-run`), while the manifest records hashes only for reviewed assets.

evidence.note: r11 is M1 (T8103) only: HEVC 144/147, AVC 73/135, opt-in High 10 FRExt 27/69 and VP9 216/305, with exact pass sets pinned. The manifest adds why each remaining failure is expected and how to acquire the input.
